key_insight: Raising cold spray pressure from 30 to 60 bar increases copper particle velocity past the critical bonding threshold, producing denser deposits with better conductivity and ductility through stronger inter-particle bonding and microstructural refinement.
engineering_relevance: For CSAM copper parts, spray pressure is a key control knob to balance electrical performance and mechanical integrity without melting the material.
method: Cold-sprayed copper at 30, 40, 50, and 60 bar using a LightSPEE3D system
Characterised deposits with XRD, SEM, hardness, eddy current conductivity, and tensile testing
Compared pressure-driven changes in particle velocity, microstructure, and fracture behaviour
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that higher pressure correlated with refined crystallites, increased dislocation density, higher conductivity, lower hardness, and a clear shift toward more ductile tensile fracture.
watch_item: The best property balance depends on staying within the higher-pressure processing window, since over-processing may reduce hardness and the results are specific to the tested system and copper feedstock.
paper_title: Optimising Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing: Pressure-driven enhancement of mechanical performance in copper deposits
